dossiers.label: The oracle: no one is wiser
dossiers.about: Chaerephon asked at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and the Pythia said no one. Socrates, knowing himself wise in nothing, tests politicians, poets and craftsmen, and finds he is wiser by this small thing: he does not think he knows what he does not know.

passage.start_quote: οὐ γὰρ ἐμὸν ἐρῶ τὸν λόγον ὃν ἂν λέγω

parts.label: Chaerephon goes to Delphi
parts.quote: εἰς Δελφοὺς ἐλθὼν ἐτόλμησε τοῦτο μαντεύσασθαι

parts.label: The Pythia: no one is wiser
parts.quote: ἀνεῖλεν οὖν ἡ Πυθία μηδένα σοφώτερον εἶναι

parts.label: I do not think I know what I do not know
parts.quote: ἐγὼ δέ, ὥσπερ οὖν οὐκ οἶδα, οὐδὲ οἴομαι

parts.label: He is wisest who knows his wisdom is worth nothing
parts.quote: ἔγνωκεν ὅτι οὐδενὸς ἄξιός ἐστι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πρὸς σοφίαν

echoes.why: The Meno: Socrates perplexes others because he is perplexed himself.

related.why: Delphi again: Socrates cannot yet 'know himself', as the inscription bids.
The service to the god continues as the gadfly.

en: I know that I know nothing

web.title: Apology (Plato)
web.quote: He says that Chaerephon, reputed to be impetuous, went to the Oracle of Delphi

dossiers.label: The gadfly
dossiers.about: Socrates is the god's gift to the city: like a gadfly on a great, well-bred but sluggish horse, he settles everywhere all day long, rousing, persuading and reproaching; kill him and you will sleep out the rest of your lives.

passage.start_quote: νῦν οὖν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, πολλοῦ δέω ἐγὼ ὑπὲρ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογεῖσθαι
passage.end_quote: εἰ μή τινα ἄλλον ὁ θεὸς ὑμῖν ἐπιπέμψειεν

parts.label: Attached to the city by the god
parts.quote: προσκείμενον τῇ πόλει ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ

parts.label: A great and noble horse, sluggish, needing a gadfly
parts.quote: ὥσπερ ἵππῳ μεγάλῳ μὲν καὶ γενναίῳ, ὑπὸ μεγέθους δὲ νωθεστέρῳ καὶ δεομένῳ ἐγείρεσθαι ὑπὸ μύωπός τινος

parts.label: You will sleep out the rest of your lives
parts.quote: εἶτα τὸν λοιπὸν βίον καθεύδοντες διατελοῖτε ἄν

related.why: The opposite image: Meno says Socrates numbs rather than stings awake.

web.title: Apology (Plato)
web.quote: he is the social gadfly required by Athens

dossiers.label: The unexamined life
dossiers.about: Socrates cannot keep quiet: the greatest good for a human being is to talk every day about virtue, examining himself and others, and the unexamined life is not worth living.

passage.end_quote: ταῦτα δʼ ἔτι ἧττον πείσεσθέ μοι λέγοντι

parts.label: The greatest good: to talk every day about virtue
parts.quote: μέγιστον ἀγαθὸν ὂν ἀνθρώπῳ τοῦτο, ἑκάστης ἡμέρας περὶ ἀρετῆς τοὺς λόγους ποιεῖσθαι

parts.label: The unexamined life is not worth living
parts.quote: ὁ δὲ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ

echoes.why: The last words of the Apology.

related.why: The end the verdict led to.
The examining began with the oracle.

web.title: The unexamined life is not worth living
web.quote: The unexamined life is not worth living

dossiers.label: The speech of the Laws (Crito)
dossiers.greek: οἱ νόμοι καὶ τὸ κοινὸν τῆς πόλεως
dossiers.about: Should Socrates escape? He imagines the Laws and the commonwealth of Athens confronting him: we begot, reared and educated you; you agreed, by staying, to obey us or persuade us; would you destroy us? Their words boom in his ears like the flutes in the ears of the Corybants.

parts.label: The Laws and the commonwealth come and ask
parts.quote: ἐλθόντες οἱ νόμοι καὶ τὸ κοινὸν τῆς πόλεως ἐπιστάντες ἔροιντο

parts.label: Can a city stand where judgments have no force?
parts.quote: ἐν ᾗ ἂν αἱ γενόμεναι δίκαι μηδὲν ἰσχύωσιν

parts.label: Their words boom like the Corybants' flutes
parts.quote: ὥσπερ οἱ κορυβαντιῶντες τῶν αὐλῶν δοκοῦσιν ἀκούειν

related.why: Socrates stays, and dies in the Phaedo.

dossiers.label: The Euthyphro dilemma
dossiers.greek: τὸ ὅσιον ὅτι ὅσιόν ἐστιν φιλεῖται
dossiers.about: Is the holy loved by the gods because it is holy, or holy because it is loved? Euthyphro has given only something that happens to the holy, being loved, not what it is; and his definitions walk away like the statues of Daedalus.

passage.start_quote: ἆρα τὸ ὅσιον ὅτι ὅσιόν ἐστιν φιλεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν θεῶν

parts.label: Loved because holy, or holy because loved?
parts.quote: ἆρα τὸ ὅσιον ὅτι ὅσιόν ἐστιν φιλεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν θεῶν, ἢ ὅτι φιλεῖται ὅσιόν ἐστιν

parts.label: Say what the holy is, not what happens to it
parts.quote: τί ποτε ὂν τὸ ὅσιον εἴτε φιλεῖται ὑπὸ θεῶν εἴτε ὁτιδὴ πάσχει

parts.label: Your words walk away like Daedalus' works

related.why: The Meno's statues of Daedalus, which run away unless tied down.

web.title: Euthyphro dilemma
web.quote: Is the pious (τὸ ὅσιον) loved by the gods because it is pious, or is it pious because it is loved by the gods?
